findings.title: No UI anywhere releases an assessment to students
findings.evidence: POST /api/teacher/assessments/[assessmentId]/release works (no-op POST of an already-released CAT returns 200) but a repo-wide search finds no caller. New assessments from /teacher/assignments set no releasedAt, so they are invisible to students by default. /teacher/planner renders Not released / Hidden from students rows with no action column, while /teacher states Nothing is released to students until you make it. Fixed 2026-09-18: `components/assessment-release-control.tsx` is now rendered in the planner's Release cell and the dashboard's State cell, so the read-only pill is the write path. Verified on the running app: POST to the release route returned 200 and wrote an `assessment.released` audit row, and the planner row changed from Not released / Hidden from students to Released / Visible to students since 17 Sept 2026, 21:09. Once released the control offers no action, because the API has no unrelease route.

findings.title: Marking progress renders an impossible ratio (9 / 0) beside a contradictory Submitted cell
findings.evidence: GET /teacher as dsa.teacher: DSA Section A CAT 1 shows Marked 9 / 0 with a 100% bar, and 0 / 9 for Submitted. Root cause confirmed in SQL: Submission rows = 0 while Grade rows = 9, because graded is not a subset of submitted. The planner repeats it in words: Week 2 practice set 0 submitted, 4 graded. Re-verified 2026-09-17 against the re-seeded database: still reproduces. Fixed 2026-09-18: the Marked bar now counts marks against the cohort, not against submissions, because a manual mark with no Submission row is legitimate product behaviour and graded is not a subset of submitted. `lib/teacher-dashboard-view.ts` gains `markingProgress` and the cell uses it. Verified on the running app: GET /teacher as dsa.teacher renders DSA Section A CAT 1 Marked `9 / 9` and Submitted `0 / 9` (was `9 / 0` beside a 100% bar), and no `N / 0` ratio remains anywhere on the page.

findings.title: Cohort average and every per-assessment Mean ignore Grade rows, so the page contradicts itself
findings.evidence: GET /teacher (dsa) renders Cohort average with No released marks yet and Mean on all four rows, then in the same view Cohort trend with 18 released marks. The analytics payload proves the marks exist: assessments[].average is null and attemptCount 0, while trend.markedCount is 18 and atRisk.publishedCount is 9. Dataset-dependent: demo has quiz attempts so its tile reads 58%, the manual-marked M.Tech sets look dead. Re-verified 2026-09-17 against the re-seeded database: still reproduces. Fixed 2026-09-18: the per-assessment population now unions finalized graded attempts with published Grade rows (mergeAssessmentScorePopulation in lib/analytics/cohort.ts), so a manual mark with no attempt counts and the page stops contradicting its own trend. Verified against the running app: GET /api/teacher/analytics?offeringId=courses-offering-mcse501l-a as dsa.teacher now returns attemptCount/average/passRate of 9 / 62.59 / 77.78 (CAT 2), 9 / 63.33 / 77.78 (CAT 1) and 1 / 80 / 100 (CAT 3) where every row was 0 / null before, and GET /teacher renders Cohort average 64% instead of No released marks yet. Tests: tests/analytics-assessment-scores.test.ts, tests/analytics-overview-grade-rows.test.ts.

findings.title: Classes roster counts enrolments, not students: 48 rows for 24 people, duplicates indistinguishable
findings.evidence: /teacher/classes (dsa) header tile reads Enrolled 48 / Active enrolments and the table has 48 rows for 24 distinct students (SQL: 50 enrolments, 25 students). 23BDA0001 appears twice with different averages and no offering column. Demo repeats it across its two offerings. Re-verified 2026-09-17 against the re-seeded database: still reproduces. Fixed 2026-09-18: chose one row per enrolment with an Offering column, because average, group and hand-ins are per-offering and summarising a student across two offerings would invent one number and hide the other. The header tile now counts distinct students and names the enrolment count. Verified against the running app: GET /teacher/classes as dsa.teacher renders Students 24 with hint 48 active enrolments (was Enrolled 48 counting rows); each duplicate row now carries its offering label.

findings.title: Publish results is irreversible and fires with no confirmation
findings.evidence: components/teacher-classes-manager.tsx posts to /api/teacher/offerings/[id]/results directly from onClick with no confirm or dialog anywhere in the file. The page copy itself says publishing cannot be undone and starts the retention clock, so one misclick purges a cohort after 15 days. Fixed 2026-09-18: publishing is one-way (`publishOfferingResults` stamps resultsPublishedAt exactly once and there is no route that clears it), so the button now opens a confirmation dialog that names the 15-day retention clock and states there is no unpublish action, matching the assessment release control. The copy and state live in `lib/results-publication-view.ts` and are unit-tested in `tests/results-publication-view.test.ts`.

findings.title: Analytics promises trends and at-risk students and renders neither; the payload is computed and discarded
findings.evidence: The nav and page description say Grade distribution, question quality, trends, and at-risk students. GET /teacher/analytics (demo) renders no at-risk content and no trend chart, yet the RSC payload contains the full roster (atRisk: 2 students) and the 15-week series. The dashboard At risk 2 tile is therefore a dead end, and the roster and trend queries run on every load for nothing. Re-verified 2026-09-17 against the re-seeded database: still reproduces. Fixed 2026-09-18: `components/teacher-analytics-dashboard.tsx` now renders the at-risk roster and the weekly trend from the overview it already fetched, so the At risk tile is no longer a dead end and neither read runs for nothing. Verified on the running app: GET /teacher/analytics as demo.teacher renders `At-risk students` (2 of 5 enrolled, pass line 50.0%, Demo Student Four below the line and Demo Student Five with no published work) and `Cohort trend` (15 teaching weeks, 8 released marks, chart SVG present).

findings.title: Primary selectors display raw database ids instead of labels (7 teacher screens)
findings.evidence: Full-page GET renders raw values in data-slot=select-value: /teacher/analytics shows courses-offering-mcse501l-a; /teacher/export, /teacher/groups and /teacher/assignments show demo-offering-active; /teacher/quiz-generation shows demo-assessment-group-project; /teacher/rubrics likewise; /teacher/marks shows all. findings.title: Analytics thresholds cannot clear the last override (Save is a silent no-op) and saving does not refresh the alerts it governs
findings.evidence: Proven by round-trip: PUT classAverageBelow=90 stored 90; blanking it and PUT {} returned 200 with classAverageBelow still 90, because the merge keeps an absent key. The UI would show Thresholds saved and restore the old value. Separately save() updates only local state, so the header Alerts use thresholds text and the alert card keep the old numbers until an offering switch. Re-verified 2026-09-17 against the re-seeded database: still reproduces. Fixed 2026-09-18: `thresholdDraftToSettings(draft, previous)` now sends an empty section (`{ intervention: {} }`) when the teacher blanks the last override in it — the API's merge replaces a section wholesale, which is the only way to clear one — and `AnalyticsThresholdsPanel` calls a new `onSaved` so the dashboard refetches the overview the thresholds govern. Verified live as dsa.teacher on courses-offering-mcse501l-a: 90 stored, then a blank save returned settings `{ intervention: {} }` with effective classAverageBelow back at 60, whereas the old `{}` body left 77 in place. Test: tests/analytics-settings-view.test.ts.

findings.title: No way to add, remove, or move a student

Fixed 2026-09-18: added the teacher enrolment write path POST/DELETE/PATCH /api/teacher/classes/enrollments (add, remove, move) with ownership, capacity and a soft dropped status, plus add/move/remove controls on the roster. Verified against the running app as dsa.teacher: DELETE dropped Kabir Sethi (23BDA0005) from MCSE501L Section A and the roster went 48 to 47 active enrolments; POST re-added him back to 48; PATCH moved him A to B and back. findings.title: Code-tasks page renders 5000% and 10000% coverage
findings.evidence: GET /teacher/code-tasks?assessmentId=demo-assessment-code renders Average coverage 5000% and a run cell 10000%. The field is a ratio in [0,1] (lib/code-eval/results.ts:238), the page multiplies by 100 (code-tasks/page.tsx:92,428), and prisma/seed-demo.ts:1202 stores coverage: 100. findings.title: Review queue will grade and publish a mark for a never-submitted draft
findings.evidence: listEvaluationCandidatesForTeacher filters only on rubric.isNot null with no status filter (review-queue.ts:293-298); a student saveDraft appeared in /teacher/reviews/candidates, evaluate returned 200 and accept published 15/20. Caveat (re-verification 2026-09-17): the original observation used a DRAFT Submission the audit created via saveDraft; the re-seeded database has no DRAFT submissions (all 7 seeded Submissions are SUBMITTED and there are 0 SubmissionVersion rows), so it could not be reproduced without creating one. The mechanism is unchanged: listEvaluationCandidatesForTeacher still filters only on ownership and the rubric's presence (lib/rubric-grading/review-queue.ts:293-298), with no submission-status filter. Fixed 2026-09-18: `listEvaluationCandidatesForTeacher` now filters `status: { in: SUBMITTED, LATE, GRADED, RESUBMITTED }` (DRAFT excluded) and `evaluateSubmissionForTeacher` enforces the same rule with a 409 (`lib/rubric-grading/submission-status.ts`). Verified live with a DRAFT row: absent from GET /teacher/reviews/candidates, and POST /teacher/reviews/evaluate returned 409 "Submission has not been handed in" where the audit saw 200; the probe rows were removed afterwards.

Test coverage for the queue read is the existing rubric suite.

findings.title: Submissions queue's Open action does not open the submission

Fixed 2026-09-18: the per-row Open link now carries the submission's own fragment (`/teacher/assignments#submission-<id>`) and the editor card carries the matching id, so Open lands on the clicked submission instead of the page top. Verified on the running app: GET /teacher/submissions as demo.teacher renders three distinct `#submission-...` hrefs and GET /teacher/assignments renders the three matching `id=submission-...` anchors.

findings.title: Create form's five kinds produce bare rows and there is no list, edit or delete
findings.evidence: Creating QUIZ, ASSIGNMENT, DESCRIPTIVE, CODE or GROUP_PROJECT returns 200 but writes only an Assessment row (questions=0, rubrics=0, code_tasks=0); the page shows no list of assessments and no route can modify or delete an Assessment. Tests: tests/assessment-registry-write-path.test.ts.

findings.title: Quiz AI offers every assessment kind as a generation target and attaches quiz questions to non-quiz assessments
findings.evidence: GET /api/teacher/quiz-generation returns every kind with no type filter (review-service.ts:34-52); generating into a GROUP_PROJECT returned 200 with publishedCount:1 and the student payload then showed quizQuestionCount:1 on a group project. Caveat (re-verification 2026-09-17): the target-list half still reproduces; GET /api/teacher/quiz-generation returns GROUP_PROJECT, CODE and DESCRIPTIVE assessments alongside QUIZ. The generation half could not be re-run because attaching new questions requires a provider call, outside this re-verification's scope; the generated-into-a-GROUP_PROJECT rows were the audit's and the re-seed purged them. Fixed 2026-09-18: the generation target list filters to `type: QUIZ` and `loadOwnedAssessment` — the single loader every generate/edit/publish path uses — rejects any other kind with 409, so a question can no longer be attached to a group project. Verified live as demo.teacher: a probe GROUP_PROJECT was absent from GET /api/teacher/quiz-generation and POST /api/teacher/quiz-generation returned 409 `Generated questions can only be attached to a QUIZ assessment.`; the probe was deleted afterwards. Test: tests/quiz-generation-pipeline.test.ts.

findings.title: One unpublished draft silently makes an entire quiz invisible
findings.evidence: With 3 published and 2 draft questions, GET /api/student/assessments reports quizQuestionCount:0 and starting the quiz returns 409 "unpublished draft questions", while GET /api/student/quiz-attempts reports questionCount:5, and no teacher UI exposes deliverability. Caveat (re-verification 2026-09-17): the re-seeded database has no draft questions (all 4 seeded questions are published, 0 drafts), so the mixed published/draft state could not be reproduced without generating questions, which requires a provider call outside this re-verification's scope. The mechanism is unchanged: quizDeliveryStatus still marks a quiz undeliverable when any question is a draft (lib/quiz-attempts/metadata.ts:52-56). Fixed 2026-09-18, per the owner's decision to deliver the published subset: `publishedQuizQuestions` is now the single draft/published predicate and `quizDeliveryStatus` returns the published subset, so the count a student sees and the questions they are served cannot come from two different sets. Restored a 3-published/2-draft state on demo-assessment-quiz: GET /api/student/assessments reported `quizQuestionCount: 3` (was 0), GET /api/student/quiz-attempts reported `questionCount: 3` with `canStart: true`, and starting the quiz returned 200 with exactly the 3 published questions (orders 0,1,2; the 2 drafts were absent). A quiz with zero published questions is treated as a different case from one with no questions — it stays undeliverable with its own reason, `This quiz has no published questions yet.`, because there is no content to serve. The teacher surface already shows the split: /teacher/quiz-generation renders `Drafts (N) · Published (M)` from GET /api/teacher/quiz-generation (`draftCount`/`publishedCount`), verified under the mixed state as 3 published / 1 draft, so no new page was needed. Tests: tests/quiz-published-subset.test.ts.

findings.title: Published quiz questions are permanent and per-question marks are invisible and unwritable
findings.evidence: DELETE on a question returns 405 and PATCH on a published question returns 409 "Published questions cannot be edited."; the client save body sends no points and no card displays it, so weighting is not authorable. Re-verified 2026-09-17 against the re-seeded database: still reproduces. Fixed 2026-09-18: decided per-question marks are authored before publish, because changing a published question under attempts already scored against it would silently diverge (each attempt stores its own maxScore); the marks are now shown and editable on drafts and a draft can be deleted, while a published question stays immutable with its reason returned. Verified against the running app as demo.teacher: PATCH on a published question returns 409 and DELETE returns 409 and leaves the row; a draft returned 200 for points 7 and DELETE removed it, then GET returned 404. The published set still reads 5.00 marks each. Tests: tests/quiz-question-points-write-path.test.ts.

findings.title: Rubrics can be authored where nothing will consume them and the picker offers quizzes that always fail
findings.evidence: listRubricsForTeacher has no type filter (rubric-service.ts:106-127); a rubric on a QUIZ returns 409 "A quiz is auto-scored and cannot have a rubric." while CODE and GROUP_PROJECT accept a rubric no Submission can ever use. Re-verified 2026-09-17 against the re-seeded database: still reproduces. Fixed 2026-09-18: `listRubricsForTeacher` is filtered to the types a Submission can come from (ASSIGNMENT, DESCRIPTIVE) and `upsertRubricForTeacher` rejects QUIZ/CODE/GROUP_PROJECT with a 409. Verified live: GET /api/teacher/rubrics as demo.teacher now offers only DESCRIPTIVE; POST on the CODE task returns 409 "A code task does not produce a submission a rubric can grade".

findings.title: Grading a rubric-less DESCRIPTIVE permanently blocks authoring its rubric
findings.evidence: After PUT /api/teacher/assessments/submissions published score 88, POST /api/teacher/rubrics returns 409 "Cannot edit a rubric after a grade has been published for this assessment"; the payload carries no locked flag so the editor stays editable until Save fails. findings.title: An unreleased assessment is visible and submittable on the student side
findings.evidence: demo-assessment-group-project has releasedAt NULL yet appears on demo.student1's /student/assessments and dashboard Due next, while /student/events correctly hides it because lib/student-assessments.ts:96-101 has no release filter. Re-verified 2026-09-17 against the re-seeded database: still reproduces. Fixed 2026-09-18: the reader now scopes `prisma.assessment.findMany` with `releasedAt: { not: null }` (lib/student-assessments.ts), the same predicate shape as the SN-29 fix in the student branch of `lib/gradebook-db.ts` and the calendar filter in `lib/calendar.ts`. Verified against the running app: GET /api/student/assessments and GET /student/assessments as demo.student1 no longer list demo-assessment-group-project (4 assessments, not 5), and /student renders it nowhere, matching the already-correct /student/events. **Server-side half (2026-09-18, second pass):** the _submittable_ half was still open — `app/api/student/assessments/[assessmentId]/submission/route.ts` contained no reference to `releasedAt`, so a student who knew an unreleased assessment's id could POST a submission to it directly and the row was written. The route now folds the release predicate into the assessment lookup itself (`prisma.assessment.findFirst` with the shared `releasedAssessmentWhere()`), so an unreleased assessment is refused exactly as a nonexistent one: HTTP 404 with `{"success":false,"message":"Assessment not found."}`. A 403 was rejected on purpose: `lib/assessment-release.ts` sets the convention that an object a caller may not see and an object that does not exist are reported identically, and a 403 would confirm the assessment exists — the fact SN-29 protected. Reproduced live against :3000 as demo.student1: before, POST to a temporary unreleased ASSIGNMENT returned 200 and wrote a Submission row (and POST to demo-assessment-group-project returned 409 only because of its type guard), while after the change both return 404 and write nothing, and a released ASSIGNMENT still returns 200; the temporary assessments and their submissions were deleted afterwards (0 rows). The release predicate also now has one definition, `lib/assessment-visibility.ts`, imported by lib/student-assessments.ts, lib/gradebook-db.ts, lib/calendar.ts and prisma/seed-courses.ts, instead of five hand-kept copies. **Sibling write paths (2026-09-18, third pass):** every other student write path that begins from a student-supplied assessment id is now closed. `startQuizAttempt`/`startPracticeAttempt` (`lib/quiz-attempts/service.ts`), `submitCodeForStudent` (`lib/code-eval/authz.ts` — `loadEnrolledCodeTask` is the single student-side loader) and `requestRetake` (`lib/quiz-attempts/retake-requests.ts`) fold the shared `releasedAssessmentWhere()` into their assessment lookup, so an unreleased assessment is refused exactly as a nonexistent one: HTTP 404 `{"success":false,"message":"Assessment not found."}`, matching the submission route and the `lib/assessment-release.ts` convention that an object a caller may not see and an object that does not exist are reported identically, so a 403 would confirm the object exists. The sibling **list** reads carried the same defect in read form and were filtered too — `listStudentQuizzes` (`lib/quiz-attempts/service.ts`) and `listStudentCodeTasks` (`lib/code-eval/submissions.ts`) — and the scoped `loadEnrolledCodeTask` also covers the `getStudentCodeTask`/`listStudentRuns` reads. The shared spine fixture (`tests/fixtures/spine.ts`, 47 dependent test files) had encoded the bug by creating its assessment with `releasedAt: null`; it is now released in the fixture setup, leaving every assertion unchanged (`tests/assessment-release.test.ts`, whose subject is the release action itself, restores the unreleased precondition in its own setup). Verified live against :3000 as demo.student1 with temporary unreleased probes, then cleaned up (0 remaining rows): the four POSTs above each returned 404 `Assessment not found.` with no QuizAttempt, RetakeRequest, TestRun, Submission or sandbox call written, while an otherwise-identical _released_ twin returned 200 with an `IN_PROGRESS` attempt; `GET /api/student/quiz-attempts` omitted the unreleased quiz and `GET /api/student/code-submissions` omitted the unreleased code task. Pinned by `tests/student-write-release-guard.test.ts`.
